To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we solved the first crystal structure of an RdRp of a member of the cardiovirus genus and captured the first example of an altered conformation in the active site of a picornavirus 3Dpol.
the structure of the first RdRp of the cardiovirus family has been solved and that the structure shows an altered conformation in the active site.

the structure of the EMCV 3DPOL RdRp reveals an altered conformation for a conserved motif (motif A), which is stabilized by a network of interactions involving residues strictly conserved across picornaviruses and may be modulated by different external effectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for the control of picornavirus infection.
the structural basis of the cardiovirus genome replication process and provides essential information for the development of future antivirals.

the structural characterization of a new picornaviral RdRp, which is a key enzyme in the viral life cycle, and the results obtained may be useful for the design of new antiviral therapies targeting the altered confection of motif A. PMID
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structural data obtained in this work provide a solid basis for studies on the RNA replication process in cardioviruses and, more generally, for the design of novel antivirals against picornaviruses.

the altered conformational state of motif A observed in our structures is not a consequence of the crystallization process but is rather an active conformation of the polymerase that is likely to be important for the RNA replication process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of EMCV RdRp reveals an unusual conformation of the RdRp active site, and the structural features observed may have important implications on the development of new inhibitors targeting the altered con formation of motif A.
the structure of EMCV RdRp reveals an unexpected dynamic feature in motif A, the most conserved segment in the active site of all picornaviridae RdRps.
the structure of EMCV RdRp is similar to that of other known picornaviruses, but with a different conformation of motif A, a key element for rNTP binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this altered conformation of the active-site motif A may be a good target for the development new antiviral drugs.
the altered conformation observed in motif A of EMCV 1Dpol may have important implications in the design of novel antiviral drugs targeting this motif.
the structure of motif A in the active site of EMCV 2.15 is a new target for the development and design of antiviral compounds.
